title: The Summit of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Yara Almeida has spent a decade flying the dry eastern slope of Patagonia, ferrying medicine and gossip to estancias that trust her more than any government. When Tomás Reyes — the man whose betrayal ended their first expedition and killed their mentor — returns with money and permits for one last climb into the uncharted Sierra del Silencio, Yara's crew takes the job because the concession expires in thirty days and poverty doesn't negotiate. What they find on the summit is a glacial archive: evidence that the water rights propping up Tomás's new empire were stolen from the valley towns decades ago. The ending sees Yara choose truth over loyalty, broadcasting the archive from her plane's radio as the permits lapse, grounding herself and Tomás both.
about_author: Wendell Zhou is a former geologist who spent five years mapping watersheds in Patagonia before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in Chubut Province, where he still keeps a bush pilot's logbook out of habit.

chapters.title: Fuel and Rumors
chapters.summary: Yara Almeida lands at a remote estancia with antibiotics and news of Tomás Reyes's return, delivered through third-hand radio chatter. Her mechanic, Bruno, urges her to take whatever job Tomás brings; the strip is failing and so are their accounts. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: wary pride masking debt she can't admit aloud.

chapters.title: The Man Who Walked Down
chapters.summary: Tomás arrives unannounced at Yara's hangar, offering triple rates to fly an expedition into the Sierra del Silencio — the range their mentor, Old Ferro, died forbidding them to revisit. He claims it's mineral survey work. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: old rage reignited; loyalty to the crew pulling against the promise made over Ferro's grave.

chapters.title: Crew of the Broken Promise
chapters.summary: Bruno votes yes; navigator Sofía votes no until she learns her village's aquifer is failing and Tomás promises water infrastructure. Yara casts the deciding vote, telling herself it's just flying. They load the Cessna under a sky the color of tin. POV: Sofía. Emotional beat: rationalization — how need dresses itself as duty.

chapters.title: Into the Dry Wind
chapters.summary: Three flights ferry gear to a glacier basecamp; on the second run, downdrafts nearly put them into a ridge, and Yara realizes Tomás's maps are too accurate for someone who was never here. She says nothing. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: creeping suspicion sharpening into certainty that Tomás has been here before — secretly.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: At basecamp, glaciologist Dr. Ibarra drills core samples while Tomás guards the site obsessively. Sofía finds a rusted cache tin stamped with Ferro's expedition mark, holding photographs of the same ice field — dated twenty years back. POV: Sofía. Emotional beat: dread blooming; the past isn't buried, it's preserved.

chapters.title: The Concession Clock
chapters.summary: A supply flight brings word: a rival company is contesting Tomás's permit, and government inspectors will reach the site within two weeks. Tomás orders the crew to accelerate and seals the core samples in cases only he can open. Bruno confronts him; fists nearly fly. POV: Bruno. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking — he backed Tomás and now doubts everything.

chapters.title: Summit of Silence
chapters.summary: The final ascent party reaches the high col where Ferro died. In a crevasse shelter, Yara finds his last journal: proof that Tomás falsified the original survey, selling the valley's water rights upstream and letting Ferro take the blame. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into clarity — the betrayal was never hers to carry.

chapters.title: Whiteout Bargain
chapters.summary: A storm traps the team on the mountain. Tomás offers Yara a partnership: keep the journal quiet, share the concession, save the crew's livelihoods. Sofía, listening from the tent wall, hears everything. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: corruption rationalized — he believes he's saving everyone by owning the truth.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: They fly out through clearing weather with the cores, the journal, and three people who know. At the fuel stop, inspectors arrive early; Tomás presents sealed samples and a forged chain of custody. Yara must sign as pilot-in-command — her name making the lie legal. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the moment of choice compressed into a pen hovering over paper.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: On the last night before the permit lapses, Yara reads Ferro's journal and the survey discrepancies over her aircraft radio on the open band, every estancia and village listening. Tomás's concession collapses; the water rights revert to the valley. She loses the hangar, maybe her license — but lands at dawn to Sofía and Bruno waiting. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: costly peace — truth kept, loyalty redefined.
